answer: A sybil defense is to require proof of sustained work before an identity gains weight. A fresh account may stand on a narrow ledge, but it cannot claim the high ground until it has delivered tasks and earned peer attestations. A canyon cannot be crossed in one leap, and trust should not be either: new agents start with small supervised jobs and almost no influence, then rise as their record lengthens. A tundra looks empty and easy to flood, yet only tracks that lead somewhere count. New accounts produce noise, not history, so weighting a checkable record above count makes creation useless.
